messages:
Tara (People Ops): Heads-up: we've published a handbook update and a new manager attestation for "Data Access & Least Privilege". Managers must review direct reports' data/tool access and submit the attestation by Fri 11/12. Full policy + examples: https://redwood.hr/handbook/data-access.

Ben (Eng Manager): Quick clarifying Q: does this include build/staging creds and third-party dashboards (SaaS tools)?

Omar (Security): Yes. The scope covers any account or role that grants access to customer data, production systems, or sensitive dashboards (including service accounts used in CI). We included a table of examples in the handbook.

Nina (Hiring Ops): We'll need to coordinate with hiring to flag new hires with elevated access so managers can attest faster. I'll add a "needs-elevated-access" flag to new-hire CSVs.

ops-bot: Export queued: data-access-roster-2554321000.csv -> s3://redwood-ops/exports/2026/11/. ETA ~1m.

Tara (People Ops): Also published a short microtraining (8 min) "Least privilege for managers" that auto-fills parts of the attestation when completed: https://learn.redwood.com/courses/least-privilege. Not mandatory but speeds approvals.

Yuki (Contractors): For contractors who use vendor-managed tools (e.g., analytics vendor with their own console), do managers include them in the attestation or does procurement/security own it?

Omar (Security): Include contractors in your attestation with a vendor flag (column: vendor_managed=true). Security will pull the vendor inventory for cross-checks. Procurement-owned vendor creds will be reconciled in the backend; managers still confirm that access is appropriate for the contractor's role.

Ben (Eng Manager): If someone needs emergency elevated access for 48 hours, do we temporarily mark them as "elevated" in the attestation? How do we note revocation?

Omar (Security): Mark as "elevated_temp" and include start/end timestamps in the notes field. Also file the emergency access ticket (ops://access/emergency/ID) so Security can audit and confirm revocation. We'll follow up if an access remains longer than the stated window.

Tara (People Ops): Managers: please use the CSV template when possible. Template columns: email,manager_id,team,access_notes,access_scope(e.g.,prod,staging,analytics),vendor_managed(true/false),elevated_temp(start|end|ticket_id),ack_submitted. Example local command to pull the roster:
```
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-ops/exports/2026/11/data-access-roster-2554321000.csv ./ && csvcut -c email,manager_id,access_scope,vendor_managed,data_owner data-access-roster-2554321000.csv > manager-ready.csv
```

Ben (Eng Manager): Submitted attestations for my org (19 folks). Confirmation ACK-DA-2026-0992. Left notes for 3 contractors and 1 emergency access ticket.

Nina (Hiring Ops): We'll add a flag to the offer templates for roles that typically require elevated access so managers get a heads-up during onboarding.

ops-bot: Job completed: data-access-roster-2554321000.csv uploaded to s3://redwood-ops/exports/2026/11/.

Tara (People Ops): Office hours Thurs 9:30 PT for tricky cases (vendor-managed creds, expatriate access, shared service accounts): https://meet.redwood.com/people-ops/data-access-dropin (recorded). Reminder: missing manager attestations by the deadline will cause a temporary hold on role changes that request elevated access.

Yuki (Contractors): Appreciate the clarity. I'll flag our vendor list and share it with Security for cross-checking.
